sn35.242:0.3: The Simile of the Great Log (2)
sn35.242:1.1: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Kimbila on the bank of the river Ganges.
sn35.242:1.2: The Blessed One saw a great log being carried along by the current of the river Ganges,
sn35.242:1.3: and he addressed the bhikkhus thus:
sn35.242:1.4: “Do you see, bhikkhus, that great log being carried along by the current of the river Ganges?”
sn35.242:1.6: When this was said, the Venerable Kimbila asked the Blessed One:
sn35.242:1.7: “What, venerable sir, is the near shore … what is inward rottenness?” Replies as above except the following:
sn35.242:1.8: “And what, Kimbila, is inward rottenness? Here, Kimbila,
sn35.242:1.9: a bhikkhu commits a certain defiled offence, an offence of a kind that does not allow for rehabilitation.
